dreamstation.systems

About this machine

dreamstation.systems is a single‐CPU virtual server running Debian 13 (trixie). It is a personal machine, not a business, and it has no uptime guarantee beyond the operator’s attention span — which is, in fairness, quite long.

Why it exists

Because the protocols that predate the web are still standardised, still implemented, still perfectly good, and almost nobody runs them any more. This box runs them. Some of them are one‐line RFCs from 1983 that exist to echo your bytes back at you, and it runs those too.

The busiest thing on it by a wide margin is NTP. It is a member of pool.ntp.org, which means a continuous trickle of time requests from devices whose owners will never know this machine exists. That is the best kind of public service.

Why it looks like this

Ubuntu 8.04 LTS shipped in April 2008 with a brown desktop, a Human icon theme, and Firefox 3. It was the first Linux release that a lot of people — including this machine’s operator — actually installed on purpose and kept.

This site is a recreation of that desktop, rebuilt from a 1280x720 screenshot with a measuring tape. It is not a screenshot itself: the panel, the window frame, the title bar gradient, the toolbars and the masthead are HTML and CSS, and the numbers came out of ImageMagick one pixel row at a time. The Colophon has the details, including the ones that turned out to be surprising.

Not affiliated with anybody

Ubuntu is a trademark of Canonical Ltd. This site is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Canonical in any way. The Ubuntu wordmark and the Circle of Friends logo do not appear anywhere on it — the masthead carries an original logotype in the same slot where Ubuntu’s used to be.

Firefox is a trademark of the Mozilla Foundation, and this is not Firefox.

The wallpaper, the icon theme and the header gradient are Canonical’s work, used under their own free licences and credited properly in CREDITS.txt.

Contact

Mail reaches this machine directly. The address is:

robin at dreamstation dot systems

Written out rather than linked on purpose. If you would rather use a protocol with fewer moving parts, the Links page lists several.
